text:
maria: Quick sync. After yesterday's canary we still have ambiguity about what users see vs what we record. We need a concise contract: minimal HTTP surface for customers + rich internal telemetry. Proposal: stick to conventional codes (200, 4xx, 429, 5xx), but always emit 3 headers with canonical values so console/SDKs can explain why.

anil: Agreed on conventional codes. One ask: many customers rely on body for structured errors. Can we keep body unchanged for success flows and add an `X-RW-Client-Note` header for short human-friendly hints? e.g. `X-RW-Client-Note: served fallback model (smaller)`

suzanne: Don't put semi-structured hints in body. Header is fine. SDKs should parse `X-RW-Route` headers into `response.meta.routing`. We'll add helpers in SDK to surface to app devs.

lee: Concrete header candidates: `X-RW-Route-Status: healthy|fallback|fail`, `X-RW-Route-Reason: placement|quota|upstream|policy`, `X-RW-Retry: none|immediate|backoff`. Telemetry tags to mirror: `route.status`, `route.reason`, `route.subcode`. Example:```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Route-Status: fallback
X-RW-Route-Reason: placement
X-RW-Retry: none
```

maria: Important policy: if we returned useful output we should prefer 200 (even when model downgraded). Reserve 5xx for cases with no usable output. That avoids breaking clients. :100:

anil: For 429/rate-limit we should return 429 and set `X-RW-Route-Status: fail` and `X-RW-Retry: backoff`. That keeps client expectations consistent.

suzanne: SDK semantics proposal: 
- If HTTP is 200 -> return Response object. Attach `meta.routeStatus` and `meta.retry` (strings). 
- If HTTP is 4xx/5xx -> raise typed error with `.type` = `rate_limit|quota|upstream|fallback` derived from `X-RW-Route-Reason`. If reason= fallback and body present -> treat as severity=warning instead of fatal when SDK config `treat_fallback_as_error=false`.

lee: We should define a short `route.subcode` space for telemetry only (no header) so we can debug: examples: `kv_cache_miss`, `gpu_oom`, `model_swap`. Console can expose human-friendly mapping but not raw subcodes.

maria: Console UX: show a badge per-route: green=healthy, yellow=degraded/fallback, red=failed. Add a timeline row per request with `route.reason` and `model_variant`. Alert rule examples: `percent(failed, 5m) > 3%` -> banner; `percent(fallback, 5m) > 7%` -> sticky notice but lower severity.

anil: Can we add a lightweight JSON diagnostic endpoint for customers to pull (`/diagnostics?request_id=...`) that returns structured route metadata (only for their requests)? That helps debugging without changing normal responses.

suzanne: Good idea. Auth required. Keep it rate-limited. We'll need to spec fields: `route_status`, `route_reason`, `retry`, `model_variant`, `quality_score`.

lee: Rollout plan: 1) runtime emits headers + telemetry (canary 5% traffic for 48h), 2) SDKs read headers and populate meta, 3) console consumes telemetry and adds badges/alerts. We'll monitor customer error-rate and `customer_support.tickets` tag.

maria: Action items: Anil write docs + example client code; Lee add runtime mappings and telemetry keys; Suzanne update SDKs + diagnostic endpoint spec; Eng-sre to watch canary.

eng-sre-bot: scheduled canary start: add-routing-headers roll 2023-11-02T02:00Z -> 5% traffic for 48h :satellite:

suzanne: I'll add tests asserting header presence for all success/fail permutations.
anil: Drafting docs, will link PR when ready.
maria: thanks all. We'll reconvene after first canary day for quick sync.
